_note: wisegraph tradition graph v1. kind: family (top level, the site's tradition filter) > school > lineage. parent is a node id. Wikidata ids checked via wbsearchentities 2026-10-20; null = no clean item.

nodes.label: Buddhism
nodes.blurb: The path of the Buddha: seeing suffering, its cause in craving, and its ending, through virtue, meditation and wisdom.

nodes.label: Theravāda
nodes.blurb: The oldest surviving Buddhist school, rooted in the Pāli discourses and the monastic code; strong today in Sri Lanka and Southeast Asia.

nodes.label: Early suttas
nodes.blurb: Practice read straight from the early discourses, outside the commentarial mainstream; Hillside Hermitage belongs here, drawing on Ñāṇavīra Thera.

nodes.label: Thai Forest
nodes.blurb: The forest monastic lineage of Ajahn Mun and Ajahn Chah.

nodes.label: Insight meditation
nodes.blurb: The modern vipassanā movement and its Western retreat centres.

nodes.label: Mahāyāna
nodes.blurb: The "great vehicle": the bodhisattva ideal of awakening for the sake of all beings, and the teaching of emptiness.

nodes.label: Zen
nodes.blurb: Chan and Zen: awakening through sitting, direct pointing and the teacher–student encounter, more than through scripture.

nodes.label: Vajrayāna
nodes.blurb: Tantric Buddhism: deity practice, mantra and the teacher's transmission as a swift path to awakening.

nodes.label: Tibetan Buddhism
nodes.blurb: The Buddhism of the Himalaya, joining monastic study and debate with Vajrayāna practice and guidance for the dying.

nodes.label: Hindu traditions
nodes.blurb: The many paths that grew from the Vedas and Upanishads: knowledge, devotion, yoga and action.

nodes.label: Vedānta
nodes.blurb: Philosophy built on the Upanishads, the Bhagavad Gītā and the Brahma Sūtras, asking how the self relates to Brahman.

nodes.label: Advaita Vedānta
nodes.blurb: Non-dual Vedānta: the Self (ātman) is Brahman, and the world of separate selves is an appearance.

nodes.label: Inchegeri Sampradaya
nodes.blurb: The Navnath line of Siddharameshwar and Nisargadatta Maharaj.

nodes.label: Ramakrishna Order
nodes.blurb: The monastic order founded on Ramakrishna's teaching and Vivekananda's mission: Vedānta lived as service.

nodes.label: Kashmir Shaivism
nodes.blurb: A non-dual Tantric philosophy in which the world is the free, conscious play of Shiva, recognised as one's own self.

nodes.label: Kriya Yoga
nodes.blurb: The line of Mahavatar Babaji, Lahiri Mahasaya and Paramahansa Yogananda.

nodes.label: Christian traditions
nodes.blurb: The traditions that follow Jesus of Nazareth, from the Gospels and the early Church to the mystics.

nodes.label: Christian mysticism
nodes.blurb: Christians who sought direct union with God: detachment, contemplative prayer and the birth of God in the soul.

nodes.label: Gnosticism
nodes.blurb: Early Christian and related movements of saving knowledge (gnosis); known mostly through texts such as the Nag Hammadi library.

nodes.label: Platonic tradition
nodes.blurb: Philosophy as the care of the soul, turning from the world of change toward the eternal Forms and the Good.

nodes.label: Neoplatonism
nodes.blurb: Late antique Platonism: everything flows from the One, and the soul can return to it through contemplation.

nodes.label: Renaissance Platonism
nodes.blurb: The revival of Plato and Plotinus in fifteenth-century Florence, joining Platonic philosophy with Christian faith.

nodes.label: Western esotericism
nodes.blurb: Western paths of hidden knowledge: Hermeticism, Theosophy, Anthroposophy and the Fourth Way.

nodes.label: Theosophy
nodes.blurb: The movement of Blavatsky and the Theosophical Society, joining Eastern ideas of karma and rebirth with Western occultism.

nodes.label: Anthroposophy
nodes.blurb: Rudolf Steiner's spiritual science: a path of clear thinking toward knowledge of spiritual worlds, karma and repeated earth lives.

nodes.label: The Fourth Way
nodes.blurb: Gurdjieff's path of self-remembering and conscious effort in the middle of ordinary life.

nodes.label: Independent
nodes.blurb: Teachers who stand outside any tradition.

nodes.label: Direct path
nodes.blurb: The non-dual enquiry into experience taught by Atmananda Krishna Menon and carried on by Jean Klein, Francis Lucille and Rupert Spira.

nodes.label: Arsha Vidya
nodes.blurb: Traditional teaching of Advaita Vedanta through the texts, in the line of Swami Dayananda Saraswati (Arsha Vidya Gurukulam, Q4796497).

nodes.label: Modern non-dual teachers
nodes.blurb: Contemporary teachers of awakening who draw on Zen, Advaita and other sources without belonging to one lineage.

nodes.label: Plum Village
nodes.blurb: Thich Nhat Hanh's Vietnamese Thiền community of engaged, mindful living.

nodes.label: Sōtō Zen
nodes.blurb: Dōgen's school of just-sitting (shikantaza); San Francisco Zen Center, Sanshin.

nodes.label: Rinzai Zen
nodes.blurb: The koan school of Japanese Zen; Zen Studies Society.

nodes.label: Gelug
nodes.blurb: The Tibetan school of Tsongkhapa, headed in practice by the Dalai Lamas.

nodes.label: Burmese meditation lineages
nodes.blurb: Myanmar's modern meditation schools: Mahasi noting, Pa-Auk samatha-vipassanā, U Ba Khin and Goenka.

nodes.label: Krishnamurti
nodes.blurb: J. Krishnamurti's teaching after he left Theosophy in 1929: no path, no authority, freedom from the known.

nodes.label: Anandamayi Ma Sangha
nodes.blurb: The ashrams and monastics around Anandamayi Ma (Shree Shree Anandamayee Sangha, Kankhal and Varanasi), devotional and non-sectarian.

nodes.label: Divine Life Society
nodes.blurb: The order founded by Swami Sivananda in Rishikesh, carried on by Swami Chidananda.

nodes.label: Siddha Yoga
nodes.blurb: Guru-yoga path founded by Swami Muktananda in the line of Bhagawan Nityananda: shaktipat, chanting and meditation, drawing on Kashmir Shaiva texts.

nodes.label: Goenka Vipassana (U Ba Khin line)
nodes.blurb: Lay Vipassana in the line of Ledi Sayadaw, Saya Thetgyi and U Ba Khin, taught by S. N. Goenka in 10-day dana-funded courses.

nodes.label: Kagyu
nodes.blurb: Tibetan school of the mahamudra lineage from Tilopa and Naropa through Marpa and Milarepa, led by the Karmapas.

nodes.label: Nyingma
nodes.blurb: The oldest Tibetan school, tracing to Padmasambhava, home of Dzogchen.

nodes.label: Sufism
nodes.blurb: The inner, mystical path of Islam: remembrance of God (dhikr), the master and the order, the poetry of love.

nodes.label: Jewish mysticism
nodes.blurb: Merkavah, Kabbalah, the Zohar and Hasidism: the contemplative and mystical currents of Judaism.

nodes.label: Philosophy of the sacred
nodes.blurb: Contemporary philosophers and scientists on consciousness, meaning and the sacred: idealism, the divided brain, the meaning crisis, perennialism.

nodes.label: Modern Paganism
nodes.blurb: Druidry, Wicca, Heathenry and goddess spirituality: nature-centred traditions revived or founded in the modern era.

nodes.label: Sikhism
nodes.blurb: The path of the ten Gurus and the Guru Granth Sahib: remembrance of the one Name, honest work and sharing.

nodes.label: Śaivism
nodes.blurb: Umbrella for Śiva-centred traditions: the ascetic Atimārga and the initiatory Mantramārga.

nodes.label: Pāśupata (Atimārga)
nodes.blurb: Earliest Śaiva ascetic order; ash, feigned madness, provoking censure.

nodes.label: Śaiva Siddhānta
nodes.blurb: Mainstream ritual Śaivism of the Mantramārga; Sanskrit āgamas, later the Tamil Śaiva temple tradition. Kauai Aadheenam teaches a monistic form.

nodes.label: Trika
nodes.blurb: Abhinavagupta's synthesis around the Mālinīvijayottara; Tantrāloka.

nodes.label: Pratyabhijñā (Recognition)
nodes.blurb: Philosophical school: liberation as recognising oneself as Śiva.

nodes.label: Spanda (Vibration)
nodes.blurb: Śiva Sūtras and Spanda Kārikās: consciousness as pulsation.

nodes.label: Krama / Kālīkula (Mahārtha)
nodes.blurb: Kālī-centred phases (krama) of cognition; Twelve Kālīs.

nodes.label: Śāktism
nodes.blurb: Goddess-centred traditions; parent of Kaula, Śrī Vidyā and Kālī lines.

nodes.label: Śākta practice (Kālī, Kāmākhyā, Bhairavī)
nodes.blurb: Bucket for living goddess practice not tied to a single classical school (Kāmākhyā upāsanā, Linga Bhairavi, Daśa Mahāvidyā).

nodes.label: Śrī Vidyā
nodes.blurb: Worship of Lalitā Tripurasundarī through the Śrī Chakra and the fifteen-syllable mantra.

nodes.label: Nāth / Siddha Siddhānta
nodes.blurb: Nāth yogī order (Gorakhnāth); Siddha Siddhānta Paddhati; alchemy and haṭha.

nodes.label: Haṭha Yoga (premodern)
nodes.blurb: Physical-yogic methods first set out in Vajrayāna and Śaiva circles (Amṛtasiddhi, Dattātreyayogaśāstra, Haṭhapradīpikā).

nodes.label: Tantra studies (academic)
nodes.blurb: Not a tradition: a field tag for scholarly lectures (philology, history).

nodes.label: Ajahn Chah line (Wat Nong Pah Pong)
nodes.blurb: Includes Amaravati, Chithurst/Cittaviveka, Abhayagiri, Bodhinyana/BSWA, Wat Pah Nanachat, Wat Marp Jan, Wat Boonyawad, Tisarana, Birken.

nodes.label: Dhammayut forest line (Ajahn Mun → Maha Boowa / Ajaan Lee)
nodes.blurb: Note: Ajahn Dtun, listed by the brief under this line, was ordained by Ajahn Chah (Mahānikāya) and is filed under chah-line.

nodes.label: Pa-Auk (samatha-first, Abhidhamma)
nodes.blurb: No usable official English short talks found this pass.

nodes.label: Mogok Sayadaw (dependent origination)
nodes.blurb: Official channel is Burmese-language only; no English clips.

nodes.label: Sri Lankan Theravāda (forest & scholastic)
nodes.blurb: Hillside Hermitage is already deep in app (early-suttas).

nodes.label: Buddhist studies (academic)
nodes.blurb: Scholarly lineage node: edges are academic_supervisor_of.

nodes.label: Sivananda Yoga Vedanta Centres
nodes.blurb: Swami Vishnudevananda's international centres teaching his guru Sivananda's yoga.

nodes.label: Bihar School of Yoga (Satyananda Yoga)
nodes.blurb: Yoga of Swami Satyananda, disciple of Sivananda, and the Bihar School of Yoga.

nodes.label: Gaudiya Vaishnava (Chaitanya / ISKCON)
nodes.blurb: Krishna devotion in the line of Chaitanya Mahaprabhu.

nodes.label: Hindu studies (academic)
nodes.blurb: Scholarly lineage node.

nodes.label: Dzogchen (Great Perfection)
nodes.blurb: Teaching and practice lineage, not a separate institution; also held in Bön and taught across Rimé.

nodes.label: Karma Kagyu
nodes.blurb: Largest Kagyu branch, led by the Karmapas.

nodes.label: Drikung Kagyu
nodes.blurb: Founded by Jigten Sumgön.

nodes.label: Drukpa Kagyu
nodes.blurb: State tradition of Bhutan.

nodes.label: Shangpa Kagyu
nodes.blurb: Separate lineage from Niguma and Sukhasiddhi, revived by Kalu Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Mahamudra (the Great Seal)
nodes.blurb: Practice lineage at the heart of Kagyu, also taught in Gelug.

nodes.label: Sakya
nodes.blurb: Lamdre (path and its fruit) teachings; led by the Khön family.

nodes.label: FPMT (Foundation for the Preservation of the Mahayana Tradition)
nodes.blurb: International Gelug network founded by Lama Yeshe and Lama Zopa.

nodes.label: Jonang
nodes.blurb: Known for shentong (other-emptiness) and Kalachakra; suppressed in central Tibet in the 17th c. and survives in Amdo.

nodes.label: Bön (Yungdrung Bön)
nodes.blurb: Tibet's indigenous religion. It is not a Buddhist school, but it shares its institutions and Dzogchen with Buddhism. Placed here for browsing only.

nodes.label: Rimé (non-sectarian) movement
nodes.blurb: An ecumenical revival across Nyingma, Kagyu, Sakya and Jonang, not a school.

nodes.label: Shambhala
nodes.blurb: Trungpa's secular "warrior" path; Pema Chödrön trained in it.

nodes.label: Chan
nodes.blurb: Chinese meditation school, root of Zen, Seon and Thiền.

nodes.label: Linji (Rinzai) line of Chan
nodes.blurb: Huatou / gong'an practice.

nodes.label: Caodong (Soto) line of Chan
nodes.blurb: Silent illumination (mozhao).

nodes.label: Dharma Drum Mountain
nodes.blurb: Taiwanese Chan organisation of Sheng Yen holding both Linji and Caodong lines.

nodes.label: Sanbo Zen (Sanbo Kyodan)
nodes.blurb: Lay-oriented school combining Soto and Rinzai koan curricula.

nodes.label: White Plum Asanga
nodes.blurb: Maezumi's lineage network (Soto with Rinzai koan study).

nodes.label: Seon (Korean Zen)
nodes.blurb: Korean Chan; Jogye order; Kwan Um School in the West.

nodes.label: Kwan Um School of Zen
nodes.blurb: International Seon school of Seung Sahn.

nodes.label: Thiền
nodes.blurb: Vietnamese Chan; Plum Village is its best-known modern form.

nodes.label: Order of Buddhist Contemplatives
nodes.blurb: Shasta Abbey tradition founded by Houn Jiyu-Kennett.

nodes.label: Ordinary Mind Zen
nodes.blurb: Joko Beck's psychologically oriented lineage.

nodes.label: Tiantai
nodes.blurb: Lotus Sutra school; threefold truth; zhiguan (calming and contemplation).

nodes.label: Tendai
nodes.blurb: Japanese Tiantai, which also includes esoteric (taimitsu), Pure Land and Zen elements.

nodes.label: Huayan (Kegon)
nodes.blurb: Avatamsaka school; interpenetration of all phenomena.

nodes.label: Pure Land
nodes.blurb: Devotion to Amitabha and rebirth in Sukhavati.

nodes.label: Jōdo-shū
nodes.blurb: Honen's school.

nodes.label: Jōdo Shinshū (Shin Buddhism)
nodes.blurb: Shinran's school; Buddhist Churches of America in the US.

nodes.label: East Asian esoteric Buddhism
nodes.blurb: Chinese Zhenyan and its Japanese heirs.

nodes.label: Shingon
nodes.blurb: Kukai's esoteric school.

nodes.label: Western magic
nodes.blurb: Ritual and initiatory magic in the Hermetic and Qabalistic line: the Golden Dawn, Thelema, the Inner Light.

nodes.label: Akbarian school (Ibn Arabi)
nodes.blurb: Study and practice centred on Ibn 'Arabi's teaching of the unity of being, as at Beshara.

nodes.label: Naqshbandi-Haqqani order
nodes.blurb: Sufi order known for silent remembrance (dhikr) and tracing its chain through Abu Bakr.

nodes.label: Inayatiyya (universal Sufism, Chishti roots)
nodes.blurb: Universal Sufism of Hazrat Inayat Khan, founded in London around 1914-1917.

nodes.label: Christian Meditation (John Main / WCCM)
nodes.blurb: Contemplative prayer with a single prayer word, taught by John Main and the World Community for Christian Meditation.

nodes.label: Franciscan contemplative (Rohr / CAC)
nodes.blurb: Followers of St Francis; in the UK including the Anglican Society of St Francis.

nodes.label: Orthodox hesychasm
nodes.blurb: Eastern Orthodox prayer of inner stillness and the Jesus Prayer.

nodes.label: Kabbalah (theosophical and ecstatic)
nodes.blurb: Jewish mystical tradition of the sefirot and the hidden meanings of Torah; also its modern popular forms.

nodes.label: Druidry
nodes.blurb: Modern Druid spirituality of nature, the seasonal festivals and bardic arts, as in OBOD.

nodes.label: Wicca
nodes.blurb: Modern pagan witchcraft publicised by Gerald Gardner from the 1950s, with covens, the Goddess and God and the wheel of the year.

nodes.label: Heathenry
nodes.blurb: Modern revival of pre-Christian Germanic and Norse religion (Asatru, Odinism).

nodes.label: Goddess spirituality
nodes.blurb: Devotion to the divine feminine as Goddess, centred in the UK on Glastonbury.

nodes.label: Hermetic Order of the Golden Dawn
nodes.blurb: Initiatory order founded in London in 1888 that shaped modern Western magic.

nodes.label: Thelema
nodes.blurb: Aleister Crowley's religious and magical system ("Do what thou wilt").

nodes.label: Quakers (Religious Society of Friends)
nodes.blurb: Christian movement begun by George Fox in 1652, worshipping in expectant silence.

nodes.label: Benedictine monasticism
nodes.blurb: Monastic life under the Rule of St Benedict.

nodes.label: Cistercians (Trappists)
nodes.blurb: Reformed Benedictines; Trappists are the Strict Observance.

nodes.label: Carmelites
nodes.blurb: Contemplative order of Teresa of Avila and John of the Cross.

nodes.label: Ignatian spirituality
nodes.blurb: The Jesuit way of the Spiritual Exercises of Ignatius of Loyola.

nodes.label: Celtic Christianity
nodes.blurb: The early Christianity of Britain and Ireland (Columba, Aidan, Cuthbert, David) and its modern revival.

nodes.label: Triratna Buddhist Community
nodes.blurb: Western Buddhist movement founded by Sangharakshita in London in 1967 (formerly FWBO).

nodes.label: New Kadampa Tradition
nodes.blurb: Movement founded by Kelsang Gyatso in England, presenting itself as independent of the Tibetan schools (Gelug-derived; contested).

nodes.label: Order of Buddhist Contemplatives (Serene Reflection)
nodes.blurb: Soto Zen order founded by Jiyu-Kennett, seated at Shasta Abbey and Throssel Hole.

nodes.label: Nipponzan-Myohoji
nodes.blurb: Japanese Nichiren order of Nichidatsu Fujii that builds peace pagodas.

nodes.label: ISKCON (Hare Krishna)
nodes.blurb: International Society for Krishna Consciousness, founded by A. C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupada in 1966.

nodes.label: Swaminarayan Sampradaya
nodes.blurb: Vaishnava tradition of Swaminarayan, including BAPS.

nodes.label: Brahma Kumaris
nodes.blurb: Spiritual movement founded in Sindh in the 1930s, teaching Raja Yoga meditation; headquarters at Mount Abu.

nodes.label: Transcendental Meditation
nodes.blurb: Mantra meditation of Maharishi Mahesh Yogi.

nodes.label: Swedenborgianism
nodes.blurb: Thought and church following the visions of Emanuel Swedenborg.

nodes.label: Spiritualism
nodes.blurb: Movement based on communication with the dead through mediums.

nodes.label: Kaula / Kula
nodes.blurb: Clan (kula) cults of yoginīs and Bhairava; source of many later Śākta and haṭha practices.

nodes.label: Franciscan contemplative
nodes.blurb: The Franciscan contemplative current: poverty and minority as a way of seeing, from Francis and Clare through Bonaventure to today.

nodes.label: Lurianic Kabbalah
nodes.blurb: The Kabbalah of Isaac Luria as recorded by Hayyim Vital: contraction (tzimtzum), the breaking of the vessels, and repair (tikkun).

nodes.label: Chishti order
nodes.blurb: The Sufi order of Muinuddin Chishti, rooted in Ajmer: music (sama, qawwali), service of the poor, and love of the teacher.

nodes.label: Qadiri order
nodes.blurb: The Sufi order of Abdul Qadir Gilani of Baghdad: sober adherence to the law joined to inward poverty and reliance on God.

nodes.label: Learned magic
nodes.blurb: Renaissance learned magic: Ficino's Neoplatonic natural magic, Agrippa's three books, Dee's angelic conversations, Bruno's heroic frenzies. Studied, not practised, here.

nodes.label: Shamanic traditions
nodes.blurb: Shamanic and plant-medicine healing traditions of the Americas, entered only where lineage, teachers and screening are verifiable.

nodes.label: Santo Daime
nodes.blurb: Syncretic Amazonian religion founded by Raimundo Irineu Serra (1930s): Christianity, South American shamanism, African animism, Kardecist spiritism. Legal churches in Oregon, Los Angeles, Washington.

nodes.label: União do Vegetal (UDV)
nodes.blurb: Christian Spiritist religion founded by José Gabriel da Costa; hoasca sacrament; US Supreme Court exemption 2006 (Gonzales v. O Centro). Núcleos across the US.

nodes.label: Shipibo curanderismo
nodes.blurb: Shipibo-Conibo plant-spirit healing (curanderismo): onanya healers, ikaros songs, dietas. Entered via its longest-running centre, not via individual claims.

nodes.label: Jainism
nodes.blurb: The Jain dharma: non-violence (ahimsa), non-possessiveness and many-sidedness (anekantavada) on the tirthankara path.

nodes.label: Taoism
nodes.blurb: The Chinese Way: Daodejing and Zhuangzi, inner alchemy, ritual and martial lineages (Quanzhen, Zhengyi, Wudang).

nodes.label: Baha'i Faith
nodes.blurb: The Baha'i Faith: unity of God, religion and humanity; no clergy, elected assemblies; Houses of Worship open to all.

nodes.label: African diaspora religions
nodes.blurb: African diaspora religions of the Americas, entered only via heritage-listed houses with published contacts.

nodes.label: Candomblé
nodes.blurb: Ketu-nation Candomblé of Bahia: orixá worship, entered via the IPHAN-listed Ilê Axé Opô Afonjá (1910).

nodes.label: Native American Church
nodes.blurb: The peyote way of the North American tribes; pan-tribal church body (NACNA). Tribally rooted, not drop-in.

nodes.label: Rigpa
nodes.blurb: Worldwide Buddhist network founded by Sogyal Rinpoche (Nyingma roots); commissioned the 2018 independent investigation into its founder.

nodes.label: Drukpa Kagyu
nodes.blurb: Drukpa (Thunder-Dragon) Kagyu of Tsangpa Gyare; Himalayan stronghold (Bhutan, Ladakh, Lahaul).

nodes.label: Drikung Kagyu
nodes.blurb: Drikung Kagyu of Jigten Sumgon; Gongchig and Fivefold Mahamudra; Drikung Thil.

nodes.label: Shangpa Kagyu
nodes.blurb: Shangpa Kagyu of Niguma and Khyungpo Naljor; the 'secret lineage', one-to-one transmission; Kalu Rinpoche its modern holder.

nodes.label: Madhyamaka
nodes.blurb: Middle-Way philosophy of Nagarjuna and Aryadeva: emptiness (shunyata) via the tetralemma; root of Mahayana dialectics and, through Chandrakirti, of Tibetan debate.

nodes.label: Vedic
nodes.blurb: Vedic religion: Samhitas, Brahmanas, Aranyakas, principal Upanishads; Rishis and the Yajnavalkya dialogues that Vedanta inherits.
